findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed no paper towels to be available at the back hand sink. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped for paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

findings.citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no food handlers license to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, ensure any employee working longer than 30 days has completed the required food handlers license and license is available within facility during all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.115: (A) Live animals may not be allowed on PREMISES of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT (B) Live animals may be allowed on PREMISE under certain conditions if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES does not occur. (C) Live or dead FISH bait may be stored if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES is prevented.

Observed a non-service animal in the bar. Cease practice. Only service animals are allowed in permitted facilities. Discussed with bartender and dog owner. COS. Dog was removed.

findings.comment:
6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. 

Observed no hand washing signs at all 4 hand sinks (back room, bar, both customer bathroom hand sinks). Provided 4 signs. Ensure all hand sinks have a sign that indicates employees must wash hands before returning to work. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food contact surfaces soiled:
1. Pizza tray and grate were soiled with pizza food debris.
2. Pizza cutting utensil on top of the pizza oven was soiled with pizza debris. Utensils should be cleaned at least every 4 hours and/or between uses.
3. Soda gun holder is soiled with mold.
4. Interior baffle of the ice machine is soiled with a layer of pink and black slimey mold. 

Discussed routine cleaning of food contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure staff is aware. Remove the ice from the ice machine and wash, rinse, sanitize the basin and baffle lip. Wash, rinse, sanitize the soda nozzle holder, pizza utensils, and pizza oven parts. Inspector will follow-u on 12/21/23.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no quaternary ammonium test strips for the sani tablets at the bar. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 12/21/23.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no copies of food handler’s licenses. Bar tender stated he has one. Ensure facility has copies of food handler’s licenses available. Discussed with PIC. Ensure new hires obtain a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Valid for 3 years. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Drink straws are observed without protection stored on the bar. PIC is instructed to either place/ handle the straws in such a way so as to protect the food and lip contact surfaces, or to acquire pre-wrapped straws. Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The deflector shield in the ice machine is observed heavily soiled with mold/slime. PIC clean the shield during the inspection to correct. Food contact surfaces need to be cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitized) often enough to prevent the growth of pathogenic organisms that could contaminate ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) The ice used for drinks in the bar area is observed without a lid or overhead protection. PIC is instructed to ensure that ready to eat foods are protected until service from falling contaminants.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) The scoop used for ice intended for drinks is observed stored with the handle in contact with the ice. PIC is instructed to store the scoop in an approved manner. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F.
